stance_summary: USD remains the cleanest benchmark after the 16 Sep 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% with the August CPI tightening bias still intact. The strongest USD spot is short AUDUSD: Australia’s housing/labor channel is biting while AUDUSD sits rich (5y 84th percentile, z 1.23) on copper at the 99th percentile and only a 26bp 2Y carry cushion. Long USDCAD has more carry (140bp) but fights WTI at $107 / 96th percentile and hotter CA activity/consumer scores. A non-USD AUD cross would add unnecessary CAD energy second-order risk.

expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated dollar-king remit is spot-only. The discrepancy lives in AUDUSD: AU housing/labor deterioration versus a still-rich AUD that is pricing copper/commodity resilience, against a USD that has just re-tightened. USDCAD is the next-best USD pair but is inferior because the 140bp 2Y gap is already large while WTI 107.02 (96th percentile, +24% 1m) and CA activity 53.2 / consumer 52.5 support CAD. AUDCAD or other crosses discard the USD/Fed leg and add CAD energy risk.

trade.thesis: FACT: Fed raised 25bp to 3.75–4.00% on 16 Sep after futures were >90% priced for the hike; August CPI is cited as keeping the tightening bias intact. US 2Y 4.76 and 10Y 5.01 are at the 99th 1y percentile (+57bp / +36bp 1m). AU 2Y 4.999 / 10Y 5.348 are also 99th 1y, but AU-US 2Y is only +25.9bp. AUDUSD 0.712022367194781 as of 2026-09-18: 1y 76th / 5y 84th, z_5y 1.23, +2.65% 3m, -0.73% 5d. NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, transaction volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak. AU labor 47.8 (U-rate 4.5% from 4.4%, employment -15.8k); AU activity 49.2 (GDP +0.4% q/q, business conditions softer); trimmed CPI 3.6% unchanged, headline 3.5% from 3.8%; Sep Westpac sentiment -5.2% to 84.4. AUD futures OI 493141, 99th 1y, z 3.61; leveraged funds net long +61135 (+11356 weekly). Copper 6.7155, 99th percentile; WTI 107.02, 96th; VIX 15.44, 15th; broad USD 118.21 stale (as_of 2026-09-11, 12th percentile). Carry screen long AUD / short USD = 26bp / 5.26 vol, ratio 0.049. Paper books are empty $100m seeds paying 5% ACT/365 on the full allocation whether flat or not. INFERENCE: AUDUSD is pricing the copper/commodity state, not the housing-labor change; the Fed path still supports the USD leg even though the 25bp decision was known. The closing mechanism is further AU housing/labor transmission and/or RBA hold-to-ease versus US higher-for-longer, which should cheapen AUD versus USD without needing a CAD or JPY second leg. UNKNOWN: RBA next decision and policy rate path; whether copper at the 99th percentile can keep AUD rich; NZ yields (unavailable); CME daily FX positioning (unavailable); broker-executable prices (ECB reference only).
trade.mispricing: AUDUSD at 5y 84th percentile / z 1.23 and +2.65% over 3m is inconsistent with a housing channel that is already cutting volumes 18% and stamp duty 24%, a 47.8 labor score, and only 26bp of AU-US 2Y carry. The market is paying for copper 99th-percentile terms-of-trade as if that dominates domestic tightening; dollar-king owns that gap in USD space.
why_now: Fed has already delivered the 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% and the retained August CPI item still flags a tightening bias, so the USD policy leg is live rather than a pre-meeting lottery.
AU housing evidence (stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, prices >7% off peak) is the new transmission of existing high AU yields, not a restatement of the rate level.
AUDUSD remains rich (5y 84th, z 1.23) after only a -0.73% 5d dip, while AUD futures open interest is at a 99th-percentile 1y extreme with leveraged funds still adding longs.
The 5% full-$100m ACT/365 clock runs whether flat or not; an empty seed book with a defined AUDUSD discrepancy should put risk on rather than donate vig with zero edge.

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if AUDUSD holds or rises while AU labor/housing stop deteriorating, or if copper/commodity strength continues to dominate without any offsetting AU domestic softening. Do not invent a numeric stop; reassess if AU unemployment reverses lower or if the Fed tightening-bias narrative is withdrawn in subsequent retained evidence.
catalysts: Further Australian housing, employment, or consumer-sentiment prints confirming the RBA tightening channel.
US inflation/labor follow-through that keeps the Fed tightening bias intact after the 16 Sep hike.
Any RBA communication that treats housing stress as a reason to stop leaning hawkish versus a still-restrictive Fed.
principal_risks: Copper at 6.7155 (99th percentile, +3.5% 1m) can keep AUD bid via terms of trade even if housing stays weak.
AUD-USD 2Y carry of +26bp slightly opposes a short; a patient squeeze can bleed if the housing catalyst is slow.
VIX 15.44 (15th percentile) is a complacent/risk-on tape that typically supports AUD.
The 16 Sep hike was >90% priced; if the residual USD bid is already in EURUSD (-1.89% 1m) and AUDUSD 5d (-0.73%), leftover edge may be small versus 5% book vig.
ECB FX marks are reference, not broker-executable; CME positioning is unavailable; broad USD is stale as of 2026-09-11.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Short rich AUD versus a just-re-tightened USD because AU housing/labor transmission is not in the 84th-percentile AUDUSD price.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next AU housing/labor/sentiment evidence versus a Fed that has already hiked and kept a tightening bias.

paper_capital.funding_hurdle_rationale: The 13 funded seats pay 5.00% simple ACT/365 on the full $100m every day whether invested or flat, about $13,699 per day / about $575k over a 6-week horizon. Flat therefore donates vig with zero edge. $35m short AUDUSD at the frozen 0.712022367194781 mark needs roughly a 1.6% AUDUSD decline over six weeks to cover that book-level clock; 20d realized vol is 4.71% and the 5y z is +1.23, so a partial unwind of the richness/housing gap can clear the hurdle without using the full $100m. Carry of only +26bp to AUD slightly opposes the short but is too small to justify staying flat. Notional is capped at $35m because copper at the 99th percentile is a real residual AUD bid.
